newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after rangebound session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after rangebound session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer on Thursday but dealings were dull and confined to less than a one cent range with much of the activity focused on rolling contracts forward from most-active July to September, dealers said.
July COMEX copper settled 0.20 cent firmer at 122.15 cents, traded 122.90 to 122.00 cents. Spot June went out 0.45 cent higher at 122.00 cents, while September fell 0.20 cent to 119.45 cents.

Prices typically peaked late in the first quarter of early in the second quarter ahead of the traditional seasonal summer slowdown, David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said, but added that the market needed evidence of easing in the current supply tightness.
"The market will continue to focus on the spreads and exchange stocks," Rinehimer said. The trend was still higher but upside potential was limited without some supply or demand shock.
LME stocks Thursday rose 825 tonnes to 123,350 tonnes.
The LME cash to three months backwardation spread widened overnight by $10 to $15, ending at $115/$120.

Meanwhile Inco Limited said talks with representatives of workers, on strike at its Sudbury mine since June 2, were due to start at 1400 EDT. The company was hopeful of a settlement emerging over the weekend, its spokesman said.
Inco, although mainly a nickel producer, also supplies copper to the U.S. Northeastern region.
